prompt: What is the exact value of $\tan 60^\circ$?
hint: Tangent is opposite over adjacent — no hypotenuse involved at all.

hints.text: Tangent is opposite over adjacent — no hypotenuse involved at all.
Opposite the $60^\circ$ angle is $\sqrt{3}$; adjacent to it is $1$.

explanation: In the $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle with sides $1$, $\sqrt{3}$, $2$, the side opposite $60^\circ$ is $\sqrt{3}$ and the adjacent side is $1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tangent can be bigger than 1
steps: Unlike sine and cosine, tangent has no ceiling — it is a slope, and slopes can be steep.
A $60^\circ$ line is steeper than $45^\circ$, so its slope must be more than 1. Only $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ qualifies; $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 0.58$ is $\tan 30^\circ$.
